description:
A freshly initialized repository excludes its machine-local `.jit/` state from version
control, so committing the store never commits lock files or checkout identity.

## Background

Discovered while executing the documented divergence recovery procedure against a fixture
built the way `jit init` builds a repository. `jit init` writes `.gitattributes` declaring
the event-log union merge, but no `.gitignore` for the machine-local set
`docs/reference/storage-format.md` names as gitignored (`.repo-write.lock`, `.events.lock`,
`.index.lock`, `worktree.json`). A plain `git add .jit/` — the recovery procedure's own
instruction, and the natural first commit of any adopter — therefore commits lock files and
the checkout's identity file. This repository does not exhibit the gap because its
`.gitignore` was authored by hand; the shipped initialization is what lacks it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: After `jit init` in a fresh repository under version control, `git add .jit/` stages no lock file and no machine-local checkout identity; the excluded set matches what the storage-format reference names as machine-local.
- [hard] REQ-02: Initialization in a repository that already carries an exclusion for these paths does not duplicate or clobber it.
- [hard] REQ-03: Coverage proves the staged-set property at the boundary an adopter uses, and the storage-format reference and init documentation agree on where the exclusion comes from.
title: Fresh init excludes machine-local .jit state from version control
